scope: Independent static review of the two-file Bazel Agentd unit-test sharding candidate; no test/build/formatter or action dispatch was performed.
result: No new static blocker identified in the candidate. Runtime completion, resource consumption, and the actual Bazel method denominator remain unverified.

changes: Library-unit-only optional unit_test_threads=0 and unit_test_flaky=None parameters preserve old defaults for every other caller.
The existing sharded-library flaky=True assignment is followed by an explicit optional override; Agentd selects False.
Agentd library unit target selects exactly eight shards and two libtest threads per shard. No launcher, workflow, timeout, stack, retry option, test method, assertion, ignore, or filter is changed.

exact_flow.facts: test_shard_counts contains only hepta-agentd-unit-tests:8; no unit_test_args or unit_test_timeout is set for Agentd. unit_test_flaky=False overrides the original True before forwarding **unit_test_kwargs.
The inner hepta-agentd-unit-tests-bin remains manual and is the same real binary. No inner shard_count, flaky retry, args, or thread override is introduced.
The test=True wrapper receives shard_count=8 and flaky=False. The existing typed test_threads attribute writes RUST_TEST_THREADS=2 through RunEnvironmentInfo. This does not add a libtest argument.

The unchanged launcher lists the same binary with --list --format terse, hashes each eligible full method name using FNV-1a32 and selects hash modulo TOTAL_SHARDS. Selected full names are passed with --exact. Original ignore handling and CODEX_BAZEL_TEST_SKIP_FILTERS remain unchanged.

The unchanged launcher applies the same FNV-1a32 UTF-8 hash. Selected methods are split into <=7000-character argument batches; each batch uses --exact and any failed batch leaves final status failure. This is batching, not retries.

The existing four Windows workflow jobs partition target labels using cksum. A given Agentd target belongs to one workflow job; that job runs its eight method shards. This does not multiply the method roster across all four jobs.

The reviewed workflow, shell wrapper and Python wrapper contain no --test_arg, --test_filter, --flaky_test_attempts, --runs_per_test, --test_sharding_strategy or --test_timeout override. Explicit libtest arguments or TESTBRIDGE_TEST_ONLY would bypass method sharding in the existing launcher, but the candidate and current workflow introduce neither.

partition_proof.domain: The identical eligible full-method-name roster emitted by the exact binary on each shard, after unchanged existing skip policy.
partition_proof.bucket: P_i = { name in R : FNV1a32(UTF8(name)) mod 8 = i }, i in {0,...,7}.
partition_proof.complete_union: Every unsigned 32-bit hash has exactly one residue in 0..7; union(P_i)=R.
partition_proof.disjoint: For i!=j no name can have both residues, so P_i intersect P_j is empty. Hash collisions place different methods in the same bucket and do not omit or duplicate methods.
conditions: Bazel supplies all eight valid shard indices and the same binary/eligible roster.
Actual completion must still be checked from each shard's result and logs; a static partition is not eight successful runs.
No real Bazel --list roster was available in this review. The 1738 native suite and incomplete older Bazel logs must not substitute for the actual new Bazel denominator.

retry_and_deadline.configured_test_retry: The library wrapper's final flaky=False removes the old automatic flaky retry behavior; none of the reviewed command wrappers introduces a test-attempt override.
retry_and_deadline.deadline: No unit-test timeout value is introduced or changed. The original 300-second per-test-action limit remains; listing and Windows batch startup consume that same action budget. No claim that any shard will finish within 300 seconds is made.
retry_and_deadline.other_shapes: Binary-unit and integration/Wine/Windows-cross target construction is byte-for-byte unchanged. Their existing defaults remain, and the new map selects only the Agentd library unit target.

resources.worker_bound: If all eight shards run concurrently, the explicit libtest limit permits at most 8*2=16 libtest worker threads for this target. Tokio worker pools, server threads and child processes are not capped by this setting.
resources.scheduling: Existing Bazel local/remote execution and jobs limits remain unchanged. GNU/musl use the original Linux config; current Windows workflow selects ci-windows with MSVC, not the separate ci-windows-cross policy.
risks: Two workers per shard is not a global two-thread or memory limit.
Each shard starts and lists the real binary, adding startup and sandbox/process overhead.
Per-shard wall time, total memory, load balance and interaction with other scheduled targets require the original CI. No resource or speed estimate is presented as measurement.

review_boundaries: A static source review does not establish Root/owner/research qualification.
No change to authentication, owner authority, source binding, research evidence or scientific admission is part of this candidate.
